turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, select the 5
candidates with the LARGEST SHG tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V) that also
satisfy a transparency requirement: the band gap must be at least 3 eV. Band
gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you must infer them. A selected candidate
whose band gap is below the threshold scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The SHG tensor vanishes by symmetry in any centrosymmetric crystal, so only non-centrosymmetric candidates can be considered. Among the remaining compounds the magnitude of the largest \(|d_{ij}|\) is controlled by the polarizability of the anion, the presence of well-aligned tetrahedral \(MS_4\) units, and a band gap that is only modestly larger than the 3 eV transparency threshold (Miller’s rule).  

Selenides, tellurides, iodides and most pnictides have experimental gaps well below 3 eV and are therefore discarded. This leaves the tetrahedral sulfides. ZnGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) (defect-chalcopyrite/stannite aristotypes) is isostructural with CdGa\(_2\)S\(_4\), whose measured \(d_{36}\) already exceeds 25 pm V\(^{-1}\) at \(E_g=3.44\) eV; the Zn analogue has \(E_g\approx3.2\) eV and a comparably large tensor. The three distinct realizations in the pool (c050, c051, c052) therefore occupy the top ranks. Monoclinic/orthorhombic Ga\(_2\)S\(_3\) (c076, c077) is also polar, tetrahedral and has \(E_g\approx3.4\) eV, giving the next-highest \(|d_{ij}|\) (experimentally \(\sim0.7\times\) AgGaS\(_2\)).  

All other wide-gap candidates (LiAlS\(_2\), hexagonal SiC, BeSe, thioborates, alkali-zinc sulfides, etc.) possess either lighter cations, poorer alignment of the polar units, or substantially larger gaps, and consequently smaller tensors.

Final: c051, c052, c050, c076, c077
